newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIAN EXOTICS - Baht unmoved by new policy measures.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN EXOTICS - Baht unmoved by new policy measures.

text.p: Thai money markets showed little immediate reaction to the new government's policy initiatives to boost the country's slowing economy on Wednesday.

The government identified the wide current account deficit as a key problem that needed to be curbed by boosting revenues and reducing spending in a policy statement to be presented to parliament later in the day.

The statement also said the government aimed to uphold fiscal discipline, further develop money and capital markets and deregulate the financial sector in stages. But it gave no time frame for the process.
Dealers said the news had little impact on baht spot or forward rates as no details were provided and there was scepticism about the government's ability to actually implement the measures.

"It's all debate and talk at the moment. There's nothing concrete in it. And if they cannot get the support of the coalition partners, they may not come through at all," said a senior trader at a Thai bank in Singapore.
He added that players might also view the measures as little more than a political ploy by Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh's party to ensure it retains the support of its coalition partners.
"If they pull out, they'd have no part to play in the government's goody bag. And I'm sure they don't want that," he said.

The baht remained near the higher end of the central bank's mid-rate, which was fixed at 25.54 on Wednesday against 25.53 on Monday. Tuesday was a public holiday in Thailand. The baht was quoted at 25.565-25.570 to the dollar at 0410 GMT.

The trader said the market would push dollar/baht down to the lower end of its trading band if the measures showed signs of being implemented. In Malaysia, the ringgit gained slightly from the dollar's overnight weakness against the majors and the U.S. unit's failure to breach a technical barrier against the ringgit.
Dealers said London players started to sell the dollar at the 2.5250 ringgit level and this spilled over to Asian trade.
"Some small funds are selling (dollar) out of Hong Kong. Apart from that there is not much liquidity," said the head of forex dealing at a foreign bank in Kuala Lumpur.
He said ringgit would remain in a range in the near-term.
"The ringgit's gains are on the back of dollar/majors' decline. The market was also caught slightly long dollar yesterday," a European bank dealer in Singapore said.
He predicted a 40-point trading range for the day.
The ringgit was at 2.5217/27 to the dollar at 0410 GMT against 2.5228/38 at close of Kuala Lumpur on Tuesday.
The Indonesian rupiah was little moved in slow trade amid adequate money market liquidity.
A European bank dealer in Jakarta said only a few Singapore operators were trading, as many investors had already covered their positions ahead of the year-end.
"Players are mostly staying on the sidelines. Corporate demand for the local currency appears to have slowed down ahead of the year-end," another bank dealer said.
Spot rupiah was quoted at 2,351.50/52.00 at 0410 GMT against an opening of 2,351.50/52.0.
Another dealer said uncertainty over the short-term rupiah liquidity outlook had kept sentiment on the local currency firm.
Dealers said they did not expect the central bank to raise its fixing later on Wednesday as it had already done so on Monday and Tuesday.
-- Madhav Reddy in Kuala Lumpur (603-230 8911), Mantik Kusjanto in Jakarta (6221-384-6364), Anuchit Nguyen in Bangkok (662-652-0642) and Sonali Desai in Singapore (65-8703090)
